correctness.rationale: The proof derives every relevant commutation equation from the presentation. For \(T=A[2]\), nonabelianity gives \(Z(G)=T\). For \(a\in A\setminus T\), one gets \(C_G(a)=A\). For \(a\gamma\notin A\), two outside elements commute exactly when their \(A\)-components differ by an element of \(T\), so \(C_G(a\gamma)=T\cup aT\gamma\), which is abelian. These equations partition the noncentral graph into one clique of size \(m-t\) and \(m/t\) cliques of size \(t\), while the center contributes \(t\) universal vertices. The isomorphism classification follows because graph order recovers \(m\) and universal-vertex count recovers \(t\). The packaged replay checks the full multiplication, centers, centralizers, and every predicted edge on multiple cyclic and noncyclic kernels.

value.rationale: The 2023 commuting-graph program explicitly studies which finite-group families yield cographs and chordal graphs, and proves adjacent generalized-dihedral and generalized-quaternion cases. The present theorem fills the natural arbitrary-kernel generalized-dicyclic gap, gives the complete graph rather than only a forbidden-subgraph label, and yields an exact graph-isomorphism classification within the family. The dependence on only \(m=|A|\) and \(t=|A[2]|\) compresses all centralizer information into two intrinsic kernel parameters and immediately transfers every graph invariant determined by the displayed cluster-join structure.
